transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess… eating has gotten kind of out of hand. Mostly at night, when I’m alone. Once I start, it feels like I can’t really stop, even if I’m telling myself I should put it away.
Do you feel guilty after these episodes of eating at night?
I don’t know… maybe. I try not to think about it too much afterward.
Do you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time during these episodes?

Yeah… sometimes. After late shifts especially, I can get through, like, a frozen pizza, some cereal, leftovers… snacks from the cabinet. It’s usually within an hour or two. More than I’d eat if anyone was around.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating during those late-night episodes?
Yeah… not really. It’s like once I start, something kind of takes over. I’ll be thinking I should stop or put it away, but I just… don’t.
Do you usually try to hide the evidence of what you've eaten during these late-night episodes?
I don’t know… I mean, I clean up after myself, but I’m not sure I’d call it hiding. I just don’t really want to leave stuff sitting out.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over time due to these eating episodes?
I don’t really know. I mean, it goes up and down a little, but I haven’t… tracked it closely or anything. Nothing I’m sure is from that.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating during these episodes?
Yeah. That’s… kind of why I came in. When I’m eating alone at night, once it starts, it feels like I can’t really stop, even if I’m telling myself to just put it away.
Do you feel like you're eating really fast during these late-night episodes?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve paid attention to the speed, exactly… it just kind of happens.
Do you usually eat at night because you're feeling stressed, anxious, or upset?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. I haven’t really connected it to a specific feeling like that. It’s usually just late and I’m by myself.
Do you think you eat at night to try to feel better when you're upset or stressed?
I’m not really sure. Maybe sometimes, but I don’t think I’m doing it on purpose to feel better. I haven’t really sorted that out.
Do you usually feel anxious or stressed right before you start eating at night?
I’m not sure. I don’t always notice what I’m feeling right before… I guess I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s anxiety or stress.
Do you think eating at night helps you deal with difficult emotions?
I don’t really know. It might, in the moment, but I haven’t thought of it that way. It’s more just… something that happens, I guess.
Do you find yourself looking forward to eating at night as a regular part of your daily routine?
I don’t know if I’d say I look forward to it. It’s not really like I plan my day around it or anything… it just kind of happens sometimes.
Do you often feel guilty or bad about yourself after these late-night eating episodes?
I don’t know… sometimes I feel kind of off afterward, but I don’t always think of it as guilt. I usually just try not to dwell on it.
Do you think eating at night makes you feel better emotionally after you've started?
Maybe a little, at first. I’m not really sure it’s emotional exactly… it’s more like I’m distracted for a bit. Then I try not to think too much about it.
Do you think you would eat this way at night if you were with other people?

No… I don’t think so. If someone else was there, I’d eat a normal amount. It’s more after late shifts, when I’m alone, I might end up eating… a frozen pizza, cereal, leftovers, snacks—just kind of a lot in an hour or two. Way more than I’d want anyone to see.
Do you think the eating at night is related to trying to cope with feelings or emotions?
I’m not sure. Maybe sometimes, but I don’t really think about it that way. It just sort of happens, and then I move on.
Do you feel like you're eating at night because you can't sleep or because you're trying to calm down?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed it being about not sleeping, exactly… or calming down. It just kind of happens sometimes.
Do you think eating at night helps you to avoid or escape from unpleasant emotions or thoughts?
I don’t know… I haven’t really connected it to that. Maybe it distracts me for a bit, but I can’t say I’m doing it to avoid anything.
Do you think your night eating is usually triggered by feeling emotional?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern like that… it doesn’t usually feel that straightforward to me.
